screen: Fitment — three new directions on one boat (second round)
job: One boat at a time, and what can be fitted to it, with everything struck through carrying the reason it was struck. Drawn on the Highfield Sport 660 (PVC · White / White / White/Blue, HBS145, boat_highfield:513, Boat Module!R863), read through src/domain/fitment/boat.ts on 2026-10-28. Motors: the boat's row says Min HP 150 HP, Max HP 200 HP, so of 209 Yamahas on sale 7 are made for it (F175XC recommended, $25,355 Cash), 30 sit inside 150–200 hp and are not made for it, 74 are under, 51 are over, and 47 twin and triple rigs are not placed. Trailers: of 434 on sale 2 are made for it (REDCO TA600T-MOB recommended, $12,643, rated 1,990 kg; GFAB tandem $24,723, rated 2,200 kg; the boat weighs 740 kg), 10 are built for another Highfield, 131 for another boat across 6 makers, and 291 name no maker; 10 more are no longer sold, said beside. Every reason sentence is say.ts's or boat.ts's own. Northside's rules refuse nothing on this boat today, so each board draws that empty state and invents no rule. The only picture is the hull's own render from above. Round 1's boards (A census, B envelope, C rig, the built one) are kept in round-1/; none of this round's references is theirs.

directions.name: D · Side by side
directions.axis: Grouped by option. The seven Yamahas made for the Sport 660 are columns, with the recommended F175XC first on its tint; the rows are facts in the dealer's units, each horsepower pinned in a 150–200 band. The other 202 are one printed sum below (7 + 30 + 74 + 51 + 47 = 209), with a numbered note for each reason.
directions.only: It answers the salesperson's next question, which of the seven that fit, side by side, while the 202 that do not fit are still accounted for, term by term, beneath.
references: docs/research/refs/fitment/live2/yachtbuyer-280-engines-table.png — the standard first, then the options as columns (only D)
docs/research/refs/fitment/live/caniemail-flex.png — numbered notes, and the printed sum 78.05% + 4.88% = 82.93% (only D)

directions.name: E · The sieve
directions.axis: Grouped by what is left. Each slot is a sieve read left to right: 209 → 162 → 111 → 37 → 7 for the motors, and 434 → 303 → 12 → 2 for the trailers. Each cut is a counted chip carrying the engine's reason, and the answer stands at the end. The pressed cut (131 built for another boat) opens a drawer of six makers, each reason said once, each with a struck example and its series banner quoted.
directions.only: It shows from across the desk how far the price list narrows for one boat — 434 trailers to 2 — as a shape, with every cut named and counted and none of it hidden.
references: docs/research/refs/fitment/live/caniuse-filtered.png with live/caniuse-has.png — one product: the pressed half is the state, and what it drops is counted here instead of an uncounted '…' (only E)
docs/research/refs/fitment/live2/yamaha-rigging-selector.png — numbered steps from the boat to the results, here already walked by the boat's own row (only E)

directions.name: F · The plate
directions.axis: Grouped by the cell that decides. The boat's own row is a dark plate: Motor 150–200 hp, one motor; Weight 740 kg; Trailer built for Highfield; and what is made for it. Each line names its cell and says what it decides. The pressed Motor line opens below as the seven made for it, in tiles, and then the other 202 by the cell that holds each one back (Max HP · 200 HP 51, Min HP · 150 HP 74, Highfield × Yamaha 30, the one-motor figures 47), each with its nearest struck example and a way into that cell.
directions.only: It traces every exclusion to the one cell of the price list that causes it, and makes that cell the thing a dealer presses to fix it — the simplest of the three, and the only one with a showpiece object.

docs/research/refs/fitment/live/abp-fishandboat.png — the plate's contents as a short list of limits (only F)
